claim: absolute difference in drive-grid mean between ant_sac_best.zip and ant_sac.zip is >= 20 return points
notes: Checkpoint selection moved the PD arm's greedy mean 98.42 points (learnings/010). Under track_eval, which averages 20 episodes per cell rather than taking a one-episode argmax, the selection effect should be smaller but not zero.
resolution_notes: |_best - _sac| = 1.60, far under the 20-point bar. Checkpoint selection moved greedy_eval's mixture mean 98.42 points but moves track_eval's drive-grid mean 1.60 - because _best is selected on single-episode MIXTURE draws, which barely correlate with a 20-episode-per-cell grid mean. track_eval is structurally more robust to learnings/010 than greedy_eval is.

claim: after ledger row 4 is appended, the standing-control guard reports a HARD-FLOOR failure (trained final_ep_rew_mean below the zero-action mean), not merely the advisory 1.18 margin failure
notes: A prediction about our own instrument, not the robot. standing-control rolls 3 zero-action episodes on the env's MIXTURE and compares against the ledger's final_ep_rew_mean. Under a mixture containing STOP, where zero action scores 909.35 by design, that comparison is ill-posed - which is why track_eval exists. STATE.md flagged the ill-posedness; this predicts the specific severity.
resolution_notes: Hard-floor failure as predicted: 'trained 43.2 vs standing 100.3 (x0.43) <- the reward is wrong, not the policy'. The metric IS ill-posed - it compares a training rollout mean (exploration noise on, ep_len 918) against a 3-episode zero-action roll over a MIXTURE containing STOP, where zero action scores 909.35 by design, which is the whole reason track_eval exists. But the verdict is substantively correct: the policy also loses on the drive grid, -6.48 against 55.73. A broken instrument agreeing with the truth is the most dangerous kind of agreement, because it is the case where nobody looks again.

claim: zero action's drive_grid_track_per_horizon equals its drive_grid_track to within 0.0005
notes: Implementation check, not a physics claim. Zero action crashed 0/120 on this grid, so every episode runs the full 1000-step horizon and the two aggregates are the same arithmetic. If they differ materially the new code is wrong, not the world.

claim: the policy's drive_grid_track_per_horizon lands in 0.060-0.069, reproducing anomaly 20's independently-derived 0.0644
notes: Anomaly 20 computed 0.0644 by hand-normalising to a common 1000-step horizon. My track_per_horizon divides each episode's Phi integral by the env's own max_episode_steps and then averages, which is the same quantity. A miss means either the anomaly's arithmetic or mine is wrong, and finding out which is the point.

claim: the length bias REVERSES the sign of the tracking verdict: raw drive_grid_track ratio > 1.4 while the per-horizon ratio is < 1.05
notes: This is the claim that matters, because cycle 007 used drive_grid_track to say the policy beats zero action on tracking. If it holds, the designated safe metric was flattering a crashing policy and learnings/011's 'reward_track essentially TIED' understates it -- length-normalised the policy LOSES on tracking.

claim: at harvest, this run's drive_grid_track and drive_grid_track_per_horizon differ by more than 10% of the smaller
notes: Forward-looking. The gap is a pure crash-rate proxy: it is zero for a policy that never terminates early. Stated at 0.45 rather than the 0.6 that felt right, because calibration reports the 40-60 band running 50% stated against 20% actual and the 80-100 band 87% against 60% -- this loop is over-confident wherever it is confident.
